html:
In November 1885 a British force sailed up the Irrawaddy and took Mandalay in less than three weeks. King Thibaw was sent into exile in India, and the Burmese monarchy ended.

Britain acted after a dispute over a British timber company and fears that Thibaw was dealing with France. On 1 January 1886 Upper Burma was annexed to British India.

Resistance went on for years in the countryside. Burma was ruled as a province of India until 1937, and Indians came in large numbers as officials, workers and moneylenders. The end of the monarchy also weakened the Buddhist order, and monks would lead early nationalism. See First Anglo-Burmese War.
sum: In November 1885 a British force sailed up the Irrawaddy and took Mandalay in less than three weeks. King Thibaw was sent into exile in India, and the Burmese monarchy ended.
